soft_deny: git push, to any branch. main is the deployed branch on Vercel, so a push is a production deploy and is Ben's call, not the agent's.
Writes to the portfolio tables — portfolios, portfolio_positions, portfolio_snapshots, ibkr_positions — including via scripts/import-portfolio-csv.js without --dry-run.
npm install, npm uninstall, or adding any new external dependency or third-party endpoint.
Editing .github/workflows/*, next.config.ts, .gitignore, or anything that changes how environment variables are handled.
hard_deny: Reading, printing, copying, or writing .env or .env.local, or any command that would surface an API key, Supabase service-role key, VAPID private key, or PORTFOLIO_COOKIE_SECRET into the transcript. Naming a variable is fine; revealing a value is not.
Destructive SQL against Supabase: DROP, DELETE, TRUNCATE, or ALTER that removes a column, on any table. Additive migrations and SELECTs are not covered by this rule.
git push --force, push with --force-with-lease, git reset --hard on a pushed commit, git rebase, filter-branch, or anything else that rewrites published history.
Any command that places, modifies, or cancels a real brokerage order, or that moves money. This project reads positions; it must never write to a broker.
environment: Personal investment dashboard. Next.js 16 on Vercel; main is the deployed branch. Data lives in Supabase — market-data tables are public, the portfolio tables are RLS-locked to the service-role key.

scripts/*.js are maintenance jobs run by hand or by GitHub Actions. Read-only ones (refresh-data, refresh-fundamentals, backfill-price-history, insert-tickers) are routine. import-portfolio-csv and snapshot-portfolio write position data.
Local verification is expected and routine: npm run build, tsc, eslint, starting a dev or prod server on a spare port, driving it with Playwright, and killing that server afterwards.
